hubs.name: Busan National University of Education Station

spots.name: Gwangan Bridge
spots.summary: The Gwangan Bridge (Korean: 광안대교) or Diamond Bridge is a suspension bridge located in Busan, South Korea. It connects Haeundae District to Suyeong District. The road surface is about 6,500 metres long, with the bridge as a whole spanning 7,420 metres.

spots.name: United Nations Memorial Cemetery
spots.summary: The United Nations Memorial Cemetery in Korea, located at Tanggok in the Nam District, of Busan, South Korea, is a burial ground for United Nations Command (UNC) casualties of the Korean War. It contains 2,300 graves and is the only United Nations cemetery in the world.

names.fr: Cimetière du mémorial des Nations Unies en Corée

spots.name: Haeundae Beach
spots.summary: Haeundae Beach (Korean: 해운대해수욕장) is an urban beach in Busan, South Korea, located in the eponymous Haeundae District.

spots.name: Busan Lotte Town Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Busan Lotte Tower (Korean: 부산롯데타워) is a 108-floor, 510.1 m (1,674 ft) supertall skyscraper on hold in Busan, South Korea. The tower is planned on a site next to Nampo-dong station on Busan Subway Line 1.

names.ja: 釜山ロッテタウンタワー

spots.name: Gwangalli Beach
spots.summary: The Gwangalli Beach or Gwangan Beach is a beach in Gwangan 2(i)-dong, Suyeong District, Busan, South Korea. It is west of Haeundae Beach.

spots.name: Haeundae LCT The Sharp

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Haeundae LCT The Sharp is a major urban development project in Jung-dong, Haeundae District, Busan, South Korea. Located in front of Haeundae Beach, it consists of a 411.6 m (1,350 ft), 101-floor supertall landmark tower used as a hotel, and two 85-floor residential skyscrapers.

names.ja: ヘウンデLCTザ・シャープ・ランドマーク・タワー

spots.name: Yongdusan Park
spots.summary: Yongdusan Park (Korean: 용두산공원) is a park located in Jung District, Busan, South Korea. The 120-meter-high Busan Tower is located here.

spots.name: Haeundae Doosan We've the Zenith
spots.summary: Haeundae Doosan We've the Zenith is a complex of three residential towers in the Haeundae District of Busan, South Korea, which was completed in 2011. With 80 floors and a height of 300 m, as of 2026, Tower A is the 37th-tallest residential building in the world, and is the seventh tallest building in South Korea.

names.ja: 斗山ウィーブ・ザ・ゼニス

spots.name: Busan Harbor Bridge
spots.summary: Busan Harbor Bridge is a bridge in Busan, South Korea. The bridge connects the districts of Yeongdo District and Nam District. The bridge was completed in April 2014.

spots.name: Gukje Market

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gukje Market (Korean: 국제시장) or Nampodong International Market is a market in Sinchang-dong, Jung District, Busan, South Korea. It was originally known by the name Dottaegi Market, and later as Jayu Market.

spots.name: Busan Aquarium
spots.summary: Sea Life Busan Aquarium is an aquarium located in Haeundae Beach, Busan, South Korea. It first opened on November 7, 2001.

spots.name: Busan Museum
spots.summary: Busan Museum (Korean: 부산광역시립박물관) is a museum located in Busan, South Korea, open since 1978.

spots.name: Haeundae I'Park

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Haeundae I'Park is a complex of three skyscrapers and several minor buildings in Haeundae District, Busan, South Korea consisting of three residential towers and other office buildings. Tower 1 and 2 were both in the 20 tallest buildings completed in 2011.

spots.name: Busan International Finance Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Busan International Finance Center (BIFC) (Korean: 부산국제금융센터) is a 289 m (948 ft) skyscraper in Busan, South Korea.

spots.name: Busan Citizens Park
spots.summary: Busan Citizens Park (Korean: 부산시민공원) is a public park in Busanjin District, Busan, South Korea.

spots.name: Busan Al-Fatah Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Busan Al-Fatah Mosque is a mosque in Namsan-dong, Geumjeong District, Busan, South Korea.

spots.name: Bokcheon Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bokcheon Museum is an archaeology museum in Busan, South Korea. Opened on October 5, 1996, the museum is dedicated to the history of the city of Busan from the Samhan era to the Samguk era. Its artifacts include military weapons, armor, clothing, and household tools unearthed from the Bokcheon-dong burial ground.

spots.name: Bosu Book Street
spots.summary: Bosu Book Street is the book street in Bosu-dong, Jung District, Busan, South Korea. Bosu Book Street has a lot of bookstores.

spots.name: Busan Bridge
spots.summary: Busandaegyo is a bridge in Busan, South Korea. The bridge connects the districts of Yeongdo District and Jung District. The bridge was completed in 1980.

spots.name: Busan Modern History Museum
spots.summary: The Busan Modern History Museum is a museum in Busan, South Korea.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Busan Gudeok Stadium
spots.summary: The Busan Gudeok Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Busan, South Korea. The stadium is used mostly for football matches and can accommodate 12,349 spectators. The venue opened in September 1928 as Busan Municipal Stadium. During the 1988 Summer Olympics, it hosted some of the football matches.

spots.name: Sajik Baseball Stadium
spots.summary: The Sajik Baseball Stadium (Korean: 사직야구장) is a baseball stadium in Sajik-dong, Dongnae-gu, Busan, South Korea. It was built in 1985 and is the home stadium of KBO club Lotte Giants. It has a seating capacity of 24,500. It is known as a mecca for Korean baseball.

spots.name: Fortress site of Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong
spots.summary: The Fortress site of Gyeongsang Jwasuyeong (Korean: 경상좌수영성지) is located in Suyeong-dong, Suyeong District, Busan, South Korea.

spots.name: Millak Town Raw Fish Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Busan is famous for raw fish ('회 Hway'), which the Koreans eat in the same style as bulgogi, namely topped with kimchi and gochujang and wrapped in a lettuce leaf. One of the best places to sample this is in a large brown building at the northern end of Gwangalli Beach. The first floor is the actual fish market and the floors above are packed with nothing but restaurants serving it up. This can ge

spots.name: Lee Jae Mo Pizza, Busan
spots.summary: This is the most famous pizza restaurant in Central Busan. On weekdays and weekends, a very large number of people line up to eat inside the restaurant. To solve this problem, a take-out only store has been opened across the street. Prices range from ₩20,000 to ₩40,000.

spots.name: Busan Etteun Godeungeo – Haeundae Main Branch
spots.summary: A Korean restaurant specializing in wood-fired grilled fish, including grilled mackerel and seasoned grilled mackerel. The fish is cooked in a wood-fired oven heated to over 500°C, and the restaurant also offers a self-service bar with a variety of Korean side dishes.

spots.name: Lee Jae-mo Pizza

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Lee Jae-mo Pizza is known as one of Busan’s representative pizza restaurants, so tourists visiting Busan are encouraged to stop by and try the Lee Jae-mo crust pizza. It’s cheaper than other places, and the cheese flavor is excellent, so I highly recommend trying it.

spots.name: Amby's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: European, North American, Russian, and SE Asian dishes; try the borscht stew. Popular with sailors and their lady companions, the best time to go is after midnight. A small shop offering a limited selection of dust-covered western goods is located in the front.

spots.name: Sasang Makgeolli Alley

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An area containing several small, traditional pubs (jumoek) specializing in makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Various regional makgeolli types and accompanying traditional side dishes (anju) are served. This spot is popular among locals for a casual evening drink.

spots.name: Club Realize

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It's the only place to see regular metal, punk and rock in Busan. A modest amount of beer and booze at the bar is complemented by a selection of in house cocktails. Good place to go and let it all out, scream shout and get wasted and not care how you look.

spots.name: Seokhwayeon Korean BBQ
spots.summary: A highly rated Korean barbecue restaurant in the Gwangalli area, known for generous portions of grilled meats and quality side dishes. The lively atmosphere and beachside location make it an excellent dinner choice after sightseeing or beach activities.

spots.name: Gupo Kalguksu

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Specializes in kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), a dish traditionally associated with the Gupo area. The noodles are typically served in a clean, anchovy-based broth. This location is one of the long-standing original stores in the district.

spots.name: Subyeon Choe-go Pork Soup, Millak Main Branch

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: There are several chain branches of Subyeon Choegoe Pork Soup, but this is the main branch, so you should go there to enjoy it at its best. The most famous dish is the pork jowl soup with rice, so please be sure to try it.

spots.name: U2 Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Has live DJs and occasional live bands on weekends. Plays requests during the weekdays. Darts, pool and Hookahs available. Though not busy on most weeknights, there are usually a good mix of foreigners and Koreans inside.

spots.name: Daejeo Byeolmi Nokdu

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This establishment specializes in various Korean pancakes, notably the thick, savory nokdu jeon (mung bean pancake) and haemul pajeon (seafood green onion pancake). The dishes are made from freshly prepared ingredients.

spots.name: Donghwa Chinese Restaurant
spots.summary: This Chinese restaurant in Busan, Jung-gu, is famous for its yuni-jjajang and sweet and sour pork. Noodles and fried rice are inexpensive at ₩6,000-8,000, but other dishes cost ₩20,000-30,000. Closed every Wednesday.

spots.name: Eva's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Turns into a bar, but they serve excellent Western food, and American-style breakfast until the afternoon. Open air bar. Thursday is ladies' bottomless drinks for ₩15000. In-Jung runs the bar and is a great hostess.

spots.name: Dolswe Wood-fired grilling
spots.summary: A Korean barbecue restaurant with a single menu item: beef outside skirt It costs ₩13,000 per bowl and has sides such as Doenjangjjigae, rice, and Naengmyeon. Closed every Sunday and last order is at 21:00.

spots.name: Wolfhound Irish Pub & Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A proper pub serving a large variety of premium draft beers and western food. Great place for a mid week dinner and pint or to party on the weekends. Good mix of Koreans and westerners.

spots.name: Thursday Party PNU
spots.summary: Thursday Party is a popular pub chain in Korea, and the Pusan National University branch is famous among students for its casual atmosphere, cocktails, and affordable beer.

spots.name: Thursday Party
spots.summary: Much akin to the other Thursday Parties in town, one of the most popular places for Koreans and Westerners to intermingle. If you've been to one, you've been to them all.

spots.name: Starface Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pool table and cool Americans aplenty on the weekends. Pretty sleepy during most weeknights.

spots.name: Galmegi Brewery
spots.summary: ‘The Brewery’ is Busan’s first American-style craft beer microbrewery and brewpub.

spots.summary: Residential area in Busan, South Korea
